quizItems.scenario: You find a child and a grandmother sharing this bedroom. Both are conscious; the grandmother cannot stand without help.
quizItems.question: Who do you assist out, in priority order?

options.text: Grandmother first, then guide the child out right behind her.
Child first, then come back for the grandmother.
Try to carry both at once.
Tell both to wait while you search the rest of the room.

quizItems.rationale: editorial-default:assist-least-mobile-occupant-first (unconfirmed with a firefighter -- see README open question) -- the child can self-evacuate with verbal guidance; the grandmother cannot move without physical assistance, so she needs you first. Leaving either behind to search further is worst.

quizItems.scenario: This corridor connects four rooms and is the only path to the stairwell from this side of the floor.
quizItems.question: Rank these actions best to worst.

options.text: Keep this hallway clear and ventilated before focusing on side rooms.
Search a side room first, then return to the hallway.
Treat it as equal priority to any single room.
Let smoke bank here while fully clearing one room first.

quizItems.rationale: A blocked single-path corridor traps every room behind it; protecting it outranks searching any one adjoining room first.

quizItems.scenario: Smoke is banking down the hallway ceiling but visibility at floor level is still clear.
quizItems.question: Rank these actions best to worst.

options.text: Stay low and continue moving toward the search objective.
Pause briefly to reassess, then continue low.
Retreat fully and wait for conditions to improve.
Stand upright to move faster through the hallway.

quizItems.rationale: Banking smoke with clear floor-level visibility is still passable low; standing upright into the smoke layer is the worst choice.

quizItems.scenario: The bathroom door is locked from the inside. You hear coughing.
quizItems.question: Rank these actions best to worst.

options.text: Force entry immediately -- an audible occupant is an active rescue.
Knock and wait for a response before forcing entry.
Look for a key elsewhere in the unit first.
Move on and note it as 'occupied, locked' for later.

quizItems.rationale: Coughing means a live, distressed occupant; moving on without acting is the worst option by far.

quizItems.scenario: An unconscious adult is on the floor between the bed and the window, closer to the window.
quizItems.question: Rank these actions best to worst.

options.text: Remove via the nearest viable exit (the window).
Drag them back out through your entry route.
Wait for a second crew member before moving them.
Search the rest of the room before moving the victim.

quizItems.rationale: Shortest path to safety for an unconscious victim wins; delaying removal to search further is worst.

quizItems.scenario: A pot on the stove has caught fire. There's a fire extinguisher on the wall and a bag of flour on the counter.
quizItems.question: Rank these actions best to worst.

options.text: Smother it with a lid or use the extinguisher.
Use the extinguisher from across the room without closing in.
Try to carry the pot to the sink.
Throw water on it.

quizItems.rationale: Smothering/extinguishing in place is safest; moving a burning pot risks spreading fire or burns; water on a grease fire causes violent flare-up and is the clearly worst option.

quizItems.scenario: The bedroom door is hot to the touch. You hear no response to your verbal announcement.
quizItems.question: Rank these actions best to worst.

options.text: Check for flashover signs (smoke color, pressure) before any entry.
Open the door slowly while staying low and ready to retreat.
Force the door open quickly to search faster.
Break a window from inside the hot room first.

quizItems.rationale: A hot door with no response is a classic flashover warning; forcing entry fast is the clearly worst move since sudden oxygen can feed a ready-to-ignite room.

quizItems.scenario: The bathroom is empty but the shower is running and the mirror is fogged.
quizItems.question: Rank these actions best to worst.

options.text: Shut off the water and widen the search to nearby rooms.
Shut off the water and mark the room cleared.
Leave the water running and move on.
Mark the whole unit cleared since this room is empty.

quizItems.rationale: A running, fogged shower means someone was here minutes ago -- widen the search rather than treating the unit as clear.

quizItems.scenario: The kitchen is clear of fire, but smoke-stained dishes suggest someone was cooking recently.
quizItems.question: Rank these actions best to worst.

options.text: Continue searching the unit -- a recently-occupied kitchen means someone may still be nearby.
Note it and search the kitchen again on the way out.
Mark the kitchen cleared and move to the next room.
Mark the entire unit cleared based on this room alone.

quizItems.rationale: Evidence of recent occupancy raises the odds of a victim elsewhere; treating one clear room as proof the whole unit is clear is the most dangerous assumption.
